newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grants Cambodia "most favored nation" status.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grants Cambodia "most favored nation" status.

text.p: The United States granted "most favored nation" (MFN) status to Cambodia after the two countries signed a bilateral trade agreement, the U.S. Trade Representative's Office said on Tuesday.

MFN status allows Cambodian goods to enter the United States at the same low tariffs as goods from most other nations. Before the agreement, Cambodia was one of a handful of countries lacking MFN privileges.
"This agreement begins a new era in trade relations between the United States and Cambodia," acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said in a statement.

"Not only will it create new opportunities for businesses in both countries, but it is an important step in Cambodia's integration into the world economy, and will advance the important task of rebuilding the Cambodian economy," she said.
The trade agreement was signed by Barshefsky and Cambodian Minister of Commerce Cham Prasidh on Friday.
In late September, U.S. President Bill Clinton signed legislation that cleared the way for granting MFN status to Cambodia.
